definition_en: to move quickly on foot, or to keep something operating
scene: 叔叔开咖啡店，他说 My uncle runs a small coffee shop to make a living.
sceneCN: 这里 run 是「经营」（第 3 个义项：让一件事持续运转）；句意：我叔叔经营一家小咖啡店谋生。

senses.title: Run: move fast on foot
senses.definition: to move quickly on foot, faster than walking
senses.example: She runs five kilometres every morning.
senses.why: Core sense: the body moves continuously and quickly along a path. Every other sense keeps either the continuity or the directed motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义：身体沿路径连续而快速地移动。其他义项都保留了“连续”或“有方向地动”这两个要素。

senses.title: Run: a machine operates
senses.definition: to operate or work, used about machines and engines
senses.example: The engine was still running when we arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到的时候发动机还在运转。
senses.why: A machine repeats the same internal motion without stopping. That repeated motion is the same 'continuous movement', moved inside the machine.
senses.whyCN: 机器不停重复内部运动；这种连续运动正是同一个“持续地动”，只是搬到了机器内部。

senses.title: Run: manage a business
senses.titleCN: 经营：让一件事持续运转
senses.definition: to manage or operate a business, organization, or system
senses.example: My aunt runs a small bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 我姑姑经营一家小面包店。
senses.why: To run a business is to keep all its parts moving and working every day. Management is the act of preventing the machine from stopping.
senses.whyCN: 经营一门生意，就是让它所有部件每天持续运转。管理就是不让这台“机器”停下来的动作。

senses.title: Run: liquid flows
senses.definition: to flow, used about rivers, taps, and other liquids
senses.example: The river runs through the old town.
senses.why: Old English rinnan meant both 'run' and 'flow'. Water moving along a channel has exactly the same continuous, directed motion as a runner.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 rinnan 同时表示“跑”和“流”。水沿水道前进，和奔跑者一样是连续、有方向的运动。

senses.title: Run: extend in a direction
senses.definition: to extend or continue in a particular direction
senses.example: The road runs along the coast for ten miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路沿海岸延伸十英里。
senses.why: A road does not move, but it presents a continuous line from one point to the next. The eye 'runs' along it, so the line is said to run.
senses.whyCN: 路不会动，但它从一点到另一点呈现出一条连续的线。眼睛沿着它“跑”，于是这条线也被说成 run。

senses.title: Run: last or continue
senses.titleCN: 持续：在时间中连续不断
senses.definition: to continue for a period of time or to have a particular length
senses.example: The play ran for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏连续上演了三个月。
senses.why: Time is imagined as a path. Something that keeps going along that path 'runs' through time; its length is how far it runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条路径。持续存在的东西在这条路径上一直走，就是“跑”过时间；它的时长就是它跑了多远。

senses.title: Run for office: compete
senses.titleCN: 竞选：在争夺中跑在前面
senses.definition: to compete in an election for a political position
senses.example: She is running for mayor this year.
senses.why: An election is a race. The candidate who 'runs' is the one moving toward the prize, and the campaign is the course.
senses.whyCN: 选举就是一场赛跑。参选者就是朝目标移动的人，竞选过程就是跑道。

senses.title: Run: colour spreads
senses.definition: to spread beyond the proper area, used about ink, dye, or colour
senses.example: The red shirt ran in the wash and stained everything.
senses.exampleCN: 那件红衬衫洗的时候掉色，把所有东西都染了。
senses.why: Dye in water moves outward along the fabric without a fixed boundary. That uncontrolled spreading is still a kind of running — motion that escapes its channel.
senses.whyCN: 染料在水里沿着布料向外移动，没有固定边界。这种不受控的扩散仍是一种“跑”——跑出了原本的水道。

senses.title: Run: publish or print
senses.titleCN: 刊登：让内容进入发行流程
senses.definition: to print or publish something in a newspaper or magazine
senses.example: The paper ran the story on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把这篇报道登在了头版。
senses.why: A printing press runs through its cycle, and the copies run off the press. Publishing a story is letting it go through that run.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机跑完一轮流程，印本从机器上“跑”出来。刊登一篇报道，就是让它走完这一轮。

senses.title: A run: a continuous series
senses.definition: a continuous period or series of something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）一段连续的时间；一连串
senses.example: The team has had a long run of wins.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍已经连赢了很多场。
senses.why: The noun keeps the shape of a line: a run is one uninterrupted stretch of events, like one continuous run along a track.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了“一条线”的形状：a run 就是事件中一段不中断的连续，就像在跑道上一口气跑完的一段。

intro.en: Run is a merger of two related Old English verbs, one intransitive and one transitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: run 由两个相关的古英语动词合并而来，一个是不可及物的，一个是及物的。年代为大致估计。

items.en: rinnan, irnan (class III strong verb) meant 'to run, flow, run together', with past tense ran and past participle runnen. A second verb, ærnan / earnan, meant 'to ride, run to, reach, gain by running'.
items.cn: rinnan、irnan（第三类强动词）意为“跑、流动、汇流”，过去式 ran，过去分词 runnen。另一个动词 ærnan / earnan 意为“骑马、跑向、到达、靠奔跑获得”。

items.en: The modern verb merges the intransitive strong verb with the transitive weak causative. The r/n metathesis explains the variant forms rinnan and irnan; the initial letters sometimes switched places.
items.cn: 现代动词把不可及物的强动词和及物的弱使役动词合并在一起。r 与 n 的换位解释了 rinnan 和 irnan 这两种变体；开头的两个字母有时会互换位置。

items.en: The ancestor is *rinnaną 'to run, flow' (German rinnen 'to flow', rennen 'to run', Dutch rennen, Old Norse renna, Gothic rinnan). The causative is *rannjanan.
items.cn: 更早的祖词是原始日耳曼语 *rinnaną“跑、流动”（德语 rinnen“流”、rennen“跑”，荷兰语 rennen，古诺斯语 renna，哥特语 rinnan）。使役形式是 *rannjanan。

items.en: Watkins derives both verbs from PIE *rei- 'to run, flow', via a nasalized form *ri-ne-a-. Boutkan and others regard this as doubtful, because the supposed related forms are poorly attested, and list the word as having no certain Indo-European etymology.
items.cn: Watkins 把两个动词都追溯到原始印欧语 *rei-“跑、流动”，经由鼻音化形式 *ri-ne-a-。Boutkan 等人认为这一说法可疑，因为假定的同源形式证据不足，因此把该词列为“没有确定的印欧语词源”。

items.en: Latin currere 'to run' gave English current, cursor, course, occur and excursion. This family is not cognate with run; it is a separate word family with the same meaning, useful for comparison but not for etymology.
items.cn: 拉丁语 currere“跑”产生了英语 current、cursor、course、occur、excursion。这个词族与 run 并不同源，只是意思相同，可供比较，但不能当作 run 的词源。

items.en: The past tense is ran and the past participle is run (unchanged). The noun run is recorded from the 14th–15th centuries. The senses 'machine operates' (1560s), 'colour spreads' (1771), 'manage a business' (1861, American English) and 'publish' (1884) all developed later.
items.cn: 过去式是 ran，过去分词仍是 run（形式不变）。名词 run 在 14–15 世纪已有记录。“机器运转”（16 世纪 60 年代）、“颜色洇开”（1771）、“经营生意”（1861，美式英语）和“刊登”（1884）都是后来发展出来的义项。

note.en: Words below can be confused with run. The notes point to sound and spelling first, then meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 run 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: the past tense of run. The vowel is /æ/, not /ʌ/, so ran and run do not rhyme.
entries.definitionCN: run 的过去式。元音是 /æ/，不是 /ʌ/，所以 ran 和 run 并不押韵。

entries.definition: a very small brown bird. It has a silent w and a short /e/, so it sounds close to 'ren', not 'run'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种很小的棕色鸟（鹪鹩）。它的 w 不发音，元音是短 /e/，听起来接近“ren”，不是 run。

entries.definition: to destroy or spoil something; also the remains of a destroyed building. It has two syllables and a long /uː/.
entries.definitionCN: 毁坏；破坏；也可作名词，表示废墟。它有两个音节，元音是长音 /uː/。

entries.definition: past tense of run. It swaps u for a, so the spelling and the vowel both change.
entries.definitionCN: run 的过去式。它把 u 换成 a，拼写和元音都变了。

entries.definition: to destroy; a ruined building. It looks like run with an extra i, but has a long /uː/ and two syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 毁坏；废墟。它看起来像 run 多了一个 i，但读长音 /uː/，而且有两个音节。

entries.definition: the past participle of ring; also one step of a ladder. It ends in -ng, not -n.
entries.definitionCN: ring 的过去分词；也可指梯子的一级。它结尾是 -ng，不是 -n。

entries.definition: a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet. The final e is silent and the vowel is long /uː/.
entries.definitionCN: 古代日耳曼字母表中的一个字母（卢恩字母）。结尾的 e 不发音，元音是长音 /uː/。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real, explainable links — real suffixes, compounds and common phrases, not made-up rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实、可解释的联系——真实的后缀、复合词和常见短语，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: runner = run + -er: the person or thing that runs.
normal.cn: runner = run + -er：跑的人或跑的东西，也就是跑步者。

normal.en: runway = run + way: the strip of ground on which a plane runs to take off or land.
normal.cn: runway = run + way：飞机用来加速起飞或降落的那条地面，也就是跑道。

normal.en: running water = water that runs: a stream or tap water that keeps moving, not still water.
normal.cn: running water = 会流的水：不断流动的溪水或自来水，而不是静止的水。

normal.en: in the long run = over a long stretch of time, as if looking down a long track.
normal.cn: in the long run = 在很长一段路程之后，也就是从长远来看。

normal.en: run out of = the supply runs until nothing is left, like a runner reaching the end of the track.
normal.cn: run out of = 供应一直“跑”到没有为止，就像跑步者跑到跑道尽头。

abstract.en: Run is a line with an arrowhead and no full stop: →→→. It insists on continuing.
abstract.cn: run 是一条带箭头、没有句号的线：→→→。它坚持要继续下去。

abstract.en: The line can lie on the ground (a road), in water (a river), in time (a run of shows), or inside a machine (an engine running).
abstract.cn: 这条线可以铺在地上（路）、放在水里（河）、放进时间里（一连串演出），或者装进机器里（发动机运转）。

abstract.en: Management and publishing are the same line seen from the side: someone keeps the process moving. Run never means 'stay'; it always means 'keep going'.
abstract.cn: 经营和刊登是同一条线从侧面看的样子：有人让整个过程持续动起来。run 从不表示“停留”，它总是表示“继续走”。

examples.en: She runs to school every day.
He runs a small bookshop in the town centre.
examples.cn: 他在市中心经营一家小书店。

examples.en: We ran out of milk this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我们的牛奶用完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 软（run）—— 跑到腿发软，还在继续跑 → run

root: 源自古英语 rinnan / irnan，核心含义为“跑、流动”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of run. One image: continuous, directed motion — along the ground, through water, across time, or inside a working machine.
sensesIntro.cn: run 的十个常见义项。一个意象：连续、有方向的运动——沿地面、穿水流、跨时间，或在运转的机器内部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: continuous, directed motion — something keeps moving along a path.
core.cn: 核心意象：连续、有方向的运动——某物沿一条路径不停向前。

branches.en: ALONG A PATH: feet, water and roads all trace a continuous line.
branches.cn: 沿路径：脚、水、道路都在描出一条连续的线。

branches.en: KEEPING IT MOVING: a machine runs by itself; a manager runs it on purpose.
branches.cn: 让它持续动：机器自己运转；管理者有意让它运转。

branches.en: LINE IN TIME: a play runs for months; a run is one continuous stretch.
branches.cn: 时间中的线：一部戏连续上演几个月；a run 就是一段不中断的连续。

branches.en: RACE AND ESCAPE: an election is a race; dye is motion that escapes its channel.
branches.cn: 竞赛与逃逸：选举是一场赛跑；染料是跑出水道的运动。

branches.en: THROUGH A PROCESS: a story goes through the press run and comes out printed.
branches.cn: 穿过流程：一篇报道走完印刷机的一轮运转，最后被印出来。

intro.en: Run is a productive verb root: suffixes and prefixes turn its 'continuous motion' into people, places, and processes.
intro.cn: run 是一个能产的动词词根：后缀和前缀把它“连续运动”的核心变成人、地点和过程。

items.meaning: a person or thing that runs
items.meaningCN: 跑步者；赛跑者（-er 表示做动作的人或物）

items.meaning: the activity of running; also continuing or in operation
items.meaningCN: 跑步；连续的；运转中的（-ing 表示动作或持续状态）

items.meaning: someone who has escaped; out of control
items.meaningCN: 逃亡者；失控的（away 表示“离开”）
items.example: The runaway horse was finally caught.
items.exampleCN: 那匹脱缰的马终于被抓住了。

items.meaning: to run or show something again; a repeated broadcast
items.meaningCN: 重播；重新运行（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The channel will rerun the series next month.
items.exampleCN: 这个频道下个月会重播这部剧。

items.meaning: to run faster than someone or something
items.meaningCN: 跑得比……快；超过（out- 表示“超过”）
items.example: No one can outrun him on this team.
items.exampleCN: 在这个队里没人跑得比他快。

items.meaning: to spread over and occupy something; to exceed a limit
items.meaningCN: 溢出；侵占；超出（over- 表示“越过、过量”）
items.example: The garden was overrun with weeds.

items.meaning: flowing or tending to flow, as a runny nose
items.meaningCN: 流动的；流鼻涕的（-y 构成形容词）
items.example: The child had a runny nose.

items.meaning: the strip where aircraft take off and land; also a catwalk
items.example: The plane waited on the runway.

items.meaning: a person or thing that came before and prepared the way
items.meaningCN: 先驱；前身（fore- 表示“在……之前”）
items.example: The telegram was a forerunner of the email.
items.exampleCN: 电报是电子邮件的先驱。
